claims.statement: The reusable-workflow OIDC guide spans all platforms, with the GHES hosted-runner exclusion; other reusable-workflow eligibility and OIDC navigation remain explicit external context.
Provider trust can restrict reusable workflows when custom job_workflow_ref is supported; standard aud/sub-only providers need supported subject customization, not assumed custom-claim support.

The source identifies GCP and Vault as custom-claim examples, allows subject customization across versions, and limits issuer customization to GHEC; provider capabilities are pinned-source context, not current cloud verification.
Standard reusable-workflow JWT claims identify the caller; job_workflow_ref identifies the called workflow, so authorization must distinguish both.
The JWT payload illustrates claim names, organization/repository/ref and called-workflow identity; sample IDs and values are not actual token observations.
Called-workflow filtering can authorize callers from an organization; that capability does not justify broadening an existing trust policy to all repositories.
The organization/called-repository filter uses a wildcard reference as an example; it is broader than exact reviewed workflow revision binding.
The specific-workflow example aims to bind a called path and SHA, but prints a space after @; retain the literal defect and use a validated whitespace-free reference in local review records.

scope: Full pinned article and literal closure read; source propositions are reference-only and do not adopt policy.
